frames.narration: The counter is 0 and two threads each run counter++. That one line is three steps: read, add 1, write. The scheduler may switch threads between any two of them.
Thread A reads the counter and keeps a private copy: 0. It has not written anything yet.
The scheduler pauses A and runs B. B reads the counter too, and it is still 0. Both threads now hold a copy that will be stale as soon as either writes.
A adds 1 to its copy and writes 1. So far this looks right: one increment applied.
B adds 1 to ITS copy (0) and also writes 1. The counter says 1, but two increments ran. One update was lost, and nothing reported an error.
Fix 1: a lock around the whole read-add-write. A takes it, B asks and has to wait, so B's read cannot happen between A's read and write.
Fix 2: one atomic add, or a compare-and-swap. If B's swap says 'only if it is still 0' and A got there first, the swap fails and B re-reads 1 and writes 2. Nothing waits and nothing is lost.
The trap: locking the read and the write separately. The lock is let go between them, so the order read, read, write, write is still possible, and the answer is still 1.
